summary: Half-open socket flood after model-variant swap causing burst 5xx and streaming drops
description:
Issue summary: Acme Health observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses and frequent streaming session drops beginning 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC following a customer-initiated model-variant switch. The spike was concentrated in eu-west and impacted active streaming chat sessions and large-embedding uploads.

Impact: ~18% elevated 5xx rate for the tenant over a 30-minute window, ~12% of active streaming sessions terminated early (socket resets). Customer reports production user-facing errors and increased latency.

Initial triage: Support escalated to SRE at 02:35 UTC after customer provided request IDs and trace samples. No scheduled platform deploys were shown in the tenant's control plane around the time of the spike; however an automated model-variant swap for the customer's pinned route completed at 02:12 UTC and triggered a tenant warmup burst.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer pins a route to a new model variant and triggers warmup/prefetch.
2) Warmup creates short-lived high-concurrency prefetch requests that flood connection pools.
3) Under sustained warmup plus concurrent customer traffic, the API gateway accept queue begins to backlog and many downstream proxies start returning 502/503.
4) Streaming sessions hit half-closed socket conditions and get reset when upstream runtime threads block on connection cleanup.

Note: We reproduced a similar failure in staging by running the customer's warmup script (prefetch=8x baseline for 30s) combined with ongoing streaming traffic at 60 concurrent streams.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Sudden warmup prefetch created a burst of short-lived connections that exposed a latent bug in connection pool pruning logic in the API gateway. The bug left half-open sockets in the ephemeral proxy (keepalive not reclaimed), creating accept_queue pressure and causing downstream runtime threads to block on socket cleanup while kvcache locks contended.

What we checked:
- apigw thread pool and accept queue metrics (elevated during window).
- proxy half-open socket counts (spike concurrent with warmup).
- runtime kvcache lock wait and prefetch latencies (elevated).
- GPU watchdog and driver logs (no driver resets observed).

Staging reproduction: By replaying the customer's warmup script while streaming 60 concurrent session simulations we observed quick growth in tcp_half_open_count and an apigw thread_pool exhaustion that produced 502s and forced runtime request cancellations. This reproduced core symptoms (502/503, streaming resets).

Root cause: combination of aggressive prefetch/warmup traffic pattern for this tenant + a connection-pruning bug in apigw that failed to reclaim half-closed sockets rapidly enough, producing accept-queue saturation and upstream request cancellations.
workaround:
1) Applied a temporary tenant-level rate cap on warmup/prefetch to smooth ramp.
2) Increased apigw accept_queue sizing for eu-west domain and tuned keepalive reclaim interval to be more aggressive.
3) Customer temporarily reduced prefetch multiplier from 8x to 2x while we validated the fix.
resolution:
Deployed hotfix 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC: apigw PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428) which:
- fixes connection pool pruning bug that left half-open sockets unreclaimed,
- improves threadpool pruning heuristics to prevent starvation under warmup bursts,
- adds a short-term mitigation to backpressure new warmup requests when accept_queue occupancy exceeds threshold.
After rollout, accept_queue occupancy dropped and 5xx rates returned to baseline for the tenant. Customer verified recovery and we kept the temporary tenant prefetch cap for 24h as a precaution.

Post-incident: change merged and monitored for 48h; no regressions observed. Incident closed 2026-03-12 after postmortem review.
follow_up_actions:
- Add a runbook section for model-variant warmup patterns and recommended tenant prefetch limits.
- Implement an automated alarm that triggers when apigw accept_queue > 70% and tcp_half_open_count rises for >60s.
- Add an integration test simulating large warmup bursts with concurrent streaming to catch regressions.
- Coordinate with product to provide guidance to customers on safe prefetch multipliers for enterprise/private tiers.
- Schedule postmortem doc and share with SRE and Solutions Engineering teams.
root_cause: Bug in API gateway connection-pruning logic combined with aggressive tenant warmup (prefetch) behavior leading to persistent half-open sockets, accept-queue saturation, and cascading upstream cancellations.
